title: Sweet and Smoky Cannabis BBQ Sauce Recipe
h1: Cannabutter BBQ Sauce: Sweet, Smoky and Easy to Dose
metaDescription: Make a sweet, smoky cannabis BBQ sauce on the stove or the grill with cannabutter and optional canna-honey, then divide it into measured portions for dosing.
excerpt: A summer cookout sauce built around dosing: simmer the base, whisk in cannabutter at the end, divide the batch into 12 portions and serve one per person at the table.
keyTakeaways: Add up the THC in the cannabutter and any canna-honey, then divide by 12 portions.
Serve infused sauce at the table in measured portions, and baste with plain sauce.
Whisk the infusion in at the end, over the lowest heat.
Refrigerate up to a week in a jar labeled with the portion size and dose.
body:
Cannabis BBQ sauce is the easy part of a summer cookout; the dosing is the real skill. Make the batch, divide it into a set number of portions and serve one per person instead of mopping infused sauce across the whole grill.

## Dosing Cannabis BBQ Sauce by the Portion

Total the THC in your cannabutter and any canna-honey, then divide by 12; the recipe card walks through an example. Spoon portions onto plates at the table rather than over shared platters, so guests skipping THC can stick to plain sauce. This sauce is strictly for adults 21 and older. It may take 2 hours to be felt, so offer one portion and wait ([setting a dose](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/)).

## Ingredients

Ketchup, cider vinegar and Worcestershire make the tangy base, molasses and brown sugar sweeten it, and smoked paprika plus a few pantry spices bring smoke and warmth. The dose comes from [cannabutter](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/), and [canna-honey](/blog/canna-honey/) can replace some of the sugar. Need flower to make either? [Order online](/shop/) from the High Society store nearest you for curbside or in-store pickup.

## Simmer and Finish

Simmer everything except the infusion gently for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring so the sugars don't scorch, and thin with water as needed. Then drop the heat to its lowest setting and whisk in the cannabutter and any canna-honey until glossy. Melting is all they need, so there's no reason to cook them longer. Cool before portioning.

## Grill-Side Option

No free burner? Simmer the base in a small, heavy pot on the cooler side of the grate, stirring often, since grill heat is harder to control. Lift the pot off before the infusion goes in. Serving it with our [infused pot roast](/blog/cannabis-infused-pot-roast/)? Count both doses, or use plain sauce on those plates.

## Storage and Labeling

Pour the cooled sauce into a jar labeled "THC" with the date, the 2-tablespoon portion size and the dose per portion. It keeps up to a week in the fridge; give it a shelf away from the everyday condiments and beyond the reach of kids and pets.

faq.q: Should I use canna-honey and cannabutter together?
faq.a: You can, as long as you add both totals before dividing. One infusion is simpler and leaves less room for error. If canna-honey is part of the sweetener, sweetness and dose are linked, so adjust the taste with plain brown sugar or molasses, never extra canna-honey.

faq.q: Can I baste meat with infused sauce on the grill?
faq.a: Better not. Basting spreads THC unevenly, some drips into the fire, and everyone eating from that platter gets a dose nobody can measure, including guests who wanted none. Baste with a plain sauce, such as a second batch of this recipe made without the infusion, then let each adult add one measured portion of the infused kind at the table.

faq.q: How long does infused BBQ sauce last?
faq.a: A week in the fridge, sealed and labeled. For longer, freeze 2-tablespoon portions in a silicone mold and bag them with the dose marked, so each cube is one portion. Thaw in the fridge and stir before serving, since butter can separate as the sauce cools.

recipe.yield: About 1½ cups (12 portions of about 2 tablespoons)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons packed brown sugar (or part canna-honey; see the dosing note)
2 tablespoons butter, split between your measured cannabutter and plain butter (see the dosing note)
steps: Whisk the ketchup, vinegar, Worcestershire, molasses, brown sugar, spices and salt in a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat and cook 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened.
Whisk in water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce reaches the texture you like.
Turn the heat to its lowest setting. Whisk in the cannabutter, plain butter and any canna-honey until melted and glossy, about 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat.
Let it cool, then divide the sauce into 12 equal portions, or store it in a labeled jar and measure each portion as you serve.
recipe.dosingNote: **THC per portion = (THC in the cannabutter + THC in any canna-honey) ÷ 12.** Figure the cannabutter's ceiling by multiplying the flower's grams by its THC share written as a decimal, then by 1,000. Example: 3.5 g of 16% flower in 1 cup of butter tops out at 560 mg, which works out to roughly 35 mg in each tablespoon. One tablespoon in this sauce, alongside a tablespoon of plain butter, puts at most about 35 mg in the batch, or about 3 mg per portion. Add 1 teaspoon of canna-honey estimated at 10 mg and the batch holds about 45 mg, nearly 4 mg per portion. Actual amounts are lower after decarboxylation and infusion losses. Start low with one portion, wait 2 hours before another, and keep the labeled jar where kids and pets can't get it.

review.summary: 14 claims checked: 13 ok, 1 fixed (0 wrong, 0 unsupported, 1 overstated); 1 ok claim also got a wording edit.

It may take 2 hours to be felt, so offer one portion and wait
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch 2026-10-24): "it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug"

claims.claim: Extended simmering can break THC down (Simmer and Finish)
claims.fix: measured THC losses come with long, high heat, and the site's own cannabutter and canna-oil recipes hold infusions at a bare simmer (180-200°F) for 3 to 4 hours; now "Melting is all they need, so there's no reason to cook them longer."
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang et al. 2016, full text via Europe PMC): extracts heated at 80-145°C for up to 60 min lost only slightly ("decreased slightly"); the "significant loss" it cites came "at longer times" at 145°C, "possibly due to evaporation"; site articles canna-butter-recipe and canna-oil-recipe (bare simmer, 3 to 4 hours)

review.notes: Independent fact-check: the CDC FAQ was reopened with WebFetch and Wang et al. 2016 was read through Europe PMC (abstract and full text). The simmering claim was also checked against the site's own cannabutter and canna-oil recipes, which hold infusions at a bare simmer for hours. High Society facts used: order online for curbside or in-store pickup; no product said to be stocked, and no phone, hours, address, payment, prices, deals or app. Writer's notes: Outline step "whisk everything, simmer" kept, with the infusion moved to the end on the lowest heat so potency is not cooked off (matches the batch's other recipes). Infused sauce served in portions at the table; basting with plain sauce only; pot-roast pairing warns to count both doses. Cross-batch sweep 2026-10-24 (orchestrator, after the fact-check workflow): The FAQ said to baste with plain sauce, but the recipe card makes only an infused batch (batch 29 fact-check note). It now names a separate plain batch, which keeps the card's 12-portion dosing math intact.
